proof:
In the separator set raw parameter and normal speeds to zero and collect the body terms of the contact coefficient. This gives the displayed density with the same contact coefficients used in the volume rows. In the regular singleton case these are the same terms with one contact per group and the proper coarea in place of the allocated coarea. All signs refer to positive inward body speed. For a proper cap cut, Gauss–Green applied to its truncated fiber has interior cut normal $-u_{ij}/\|u_{ij}\|$. Thus the captured old boundary flux equals the divergence integral over the cap plus the flux with $+u_{ij}$ integrated against the proper coarea. On an inside supporting fiber the old cap includes the full fiber, with body selector one and section selector zero. On an outside supporting fiber its volume is zero and the old outward normal on the face is $u_{ij}/\|u_{ij}\|$, so equal body and section allocations give the same rule. Strict full or empty traces and atomic rows use whole-fiber or zero flux directly. These verifications give the rule for constants and linear vector fields needed here, including endpoint counting for $d=1$.

The projective identities of d90ba05577427854 give $\int P_a^{-N}=\int P_a^{-N-1}=E_a$ and $\int X P_a^{-N-1}=E_a y_{ia}$ on the own fiber. Thus the energy vector flux is $-e_{ia}a_a$. The centered quadratic has zero vector flux on each fiber because $\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)\,dX=0$. Constants also have zero vector flux. Since positive finite-plane $L$ makes $\log L$ Lipschitz near the current hull, its first weak continuous derivative is $\nabla_X L/L$ almost everywhere and has no additional boundary term on creases. This gives the stated $F_z$.

The total cap force from group $i$ is $\kappa_i U_i$. Its base moment is $\sum_a\kappa_{ia}p_{ia}\otimes U_i$ by the allocated means. Substitute $\kappa_{ia}U_i=e_{ia}(a_a+c_{ia}/(N L_a))$. The $a_a$ terms cancel the energy contributions. The remaining gradient terms cancel the corresponding volume integrals of $\nabla_X\log L$ and $z\otimes\nabla_X\log L$ by the labeled identity with $\chi(c)=c$, multiplied by $1/N$. This proves both force sums.

For the continuous tensor, Gauss–Green for a scalar density $B$ gives $\int_{\partial K_z}B X\otimes n_z=I_d\int_{K_z}B+\int_{K_z}X\otimes\nabla_X B$, with the allocated cap version just proved. Set $C_i^u=\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T}$. The weighted section mean gives the cap moment beyond its raw volume term as $\sum_{ia}\kappa_{ia}y_{ia}\otimes U_i-\sum_i e_i\Sigma C_i^u$. The raw volume terms total $QI_d$ including the atomic rows and cancel $-\beta MI_d$. By the projective identities, the energy tensor is $\Delta I_d/N-\sum_{ia}e_{ia}y_{ia}\otimes a_a$. The covariance term has scalar part $\Delta I_d/2$ since $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, and derivative part $\sum_i e_i\Sigma C_i^u$ by the centered covariance definition and the zero centered first moment on every fiber. The constant contributes $-(N+2)\Delta I_d/(2N)$. The logarithm's scalar term is zero by $\int_S\log L\,dm=0$, and its derivative tensor is $-k\int_S X\otimes\nabla_X\log L\,dm$. The scalar coefficients sum to zero. The covariance parts cancel, and substituting the contact normal identity reduces the remaining sum to the labeled identity for $X\otimes\nabla_X\log L$. This proves the continuous tensor identity. Its trace and the definition of $F_z$ yield the centroid residual. An affine function of $z$ pairs to zero with the two force sums.

For the actual affine composition, a fiber-affine invertible map has the form $z'=Tz+b$, $X'=AX+Bz+c$, where the base map preserves the lattice and $A$ is the common continuous linear part. Transport the caps by their actual affine images and $L$ by exact pullback. The mixed mass and each energy gain the same factor $|\det A|$ by change of variables and d90ba05577427854, so $E/M$ and the mean logarithmic normalization are preserved. Centering on each fiber gives new covariance $A\Sigma A^{\mathsf T}$, and the cap's continuous covector becomes $A^{-\mathsf T}u$. The buffered margins and normalized cap masses are therefore unchanged at every parameter of the composed path. For a smooth base-fixed affine motion with continuous velocity $V_z(X)$, the margin speed on an old cap plane is $-u_{ij}\cdot V_z(X)$. At an inside supporting face $n_z=-u_{ij}/\|u_{ij}\|$ and at an outside face $n_z=u_{ij}/\|u_{ij}\|$. Hence each supporting hinge argument is zero, since its threshold-motion speed equals the inward body speed $-n_z\cdot V_z$. This calculation is at the level of actual composed paths; it needs no continuous raw parameter jet at a moving crease.

statement:
Use the common finite-contact buffered separator and its same-coefficient gradient-labeled volume rows. A regular singleton joint separator with the same body terms, the stated singleton section means and the same-coefficient volume rows is included. Let $W_z$ be the allocated boundary cap load including the atomic whole-fiber contributions. Each old cap has mass $Q=\beta M$, and the cap weights $\omega_{ij}$ and atomic weights sum to one. Define $k=\Delta/(NM)$ and
$$
\Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-\beta+\sum_{ia:p_{ia}=z}\frac{e_{ia}P_a(X)^{-N}}{NE_a}
+\frac1{2M}\sum_{ij}e_i\rho_{ij}[u_{ij}\cdot(X-g_z)]^2
-\frac{(N+2)\Delta}{2NM}-k\log L(z,X).
$$
Then $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_zv_z\,dS\le0$ on the same actual body cone. Let $S_{ij}(z)$ be the consistently allocated coarea in fiber $z$. The force and affine moments satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
F_z:=\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z n_z\,dS
&=\sum_{ij}\omega_{ij}S_{ij}(z)u_{ij}-\sum_{ia:p_{ia}=z}e_{ia}a_a
-k\int_{K_z}\nabla_X\log L\,dX,\\
\sum_z F_z&=0,\qquad
\sum_z z\otimes F_z=0,\qquad
\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z X\otimes n_z\,dS=0 .
\end{aligned}
$$
For the ordinary centroid radial array its formal response is $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_z\,n_z\cdot(X-g_z)\,dS=-\sum_z g_z\cdot F_z$, which is zero for an affine centroid graph. Exact composition of an actual path with a lattice-preserving fiber-affine change of variables, transporting the parameter and caps, preserves the normalized buffered response.
